newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close tad lower, seen static.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close tad lower, seen static.

text.p: Argentine stocks remained trapped in a tight band and closed slightly lower on Thursday, with bids petering out ahead of a 36-hour general strike, dealers said.
"The market's on the defensive and anticipating a lull Thursday and Friday," Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The trade union strike against fiscal and labor reforms starts at midday on Thursday.
After Tuesday's flat finish the blue-chip MerVal index dipped 0.2 percent to 544.37, matching broad market losses.
Floor volume shrank to 9.8 million pesos against 14.9 million on Tuesday and a nominal 5.5 million traded during the Yom Kippur Jewish holiday on Monday.

"The market is only lightly negative, but it's not strong. It's a volume problem again, which means one day could be good and one day could be bad just on the basis of one million dollars more in positive or negative bids," said analyst Christopher Ecclestone at brokers Interacciones.
Technical analysts forecast the MerVal index would pull back to technical support at around 530 as activity winds down during the strike.

"It will be interesting to see what the degree of adhesion to the strike is and that will probably affect the market," said Ecclestone. "I suspect tomorrow will not be as bad a day as Friday -- a lot of people are probably going to turn up for work tomorrow as buses will be running until 8 pm (1900 EDT)."

Public transportation is due to run normally on Thursday afternoon to help protestors take part in a mass demonstration outside government house. In the session losing issues outpaced winners 24 to 18 and 17 stocks closed flat.
Over-the-counter volume eased to 62.6 million pesos from 64.3 million on Tuesday.

The day's biggest main-tier losses were posted by carmaker Sevel, power distributor Central Costanera and construction stock Juan Minetti, which declined 4.1 percent, 3.4 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively.
MerVal gains were led by construction stock Polledo, which jumped 4.2 percent, steelmaker Acindar, which advanced 2.2 percent and oil company Sol Petrleo, up 1.7 percent.
